title: Codex Companion: unified local usage, quota, input analytics and migration
body:
Codex Companion replaces the migration-only application with one native macOS app and one Swift executable target, `CodexCompanion`. Provider migration is an integrated tool; the old executable, source directory and bundle identifier are replaced.

## Behavior

- Browse token usage by date, project, chat, model, turn and individual model request; export request usage to CSV.
- Inspect account quota windows, observed consumption in allowance equivalents, reset history and expected reset time. Chat/turn attribution is explicitly approximate and ambiguous consumption remains unassigned.
- Analyze human inputs with Chinese/English segmentation, a wrapping word cloud, searchable full word frequencies, character volume and expandable input history. App context, attachment/annotation scaffolding and question-reply metadata are excluded.
- Read active, archived and optional migration-backup logs with request/message deduplication, legacy estimate labels and explicit coverage gaps. Analytics run locally without credential reads or uploads.
- Harden migration for current storage: local-host catalog isolation, versioned/configured runtime databases, schema and selection validation, metadata-only JSON rewriting, consistent SQLite backups and WAL-safe rollback, and running-process guards.

## Validation

- Eight fixture suites pass, covering migration isolation, rollback, schemas, usage deduplication, input filtering/segmentation and quota edge cases.
- Release compilation, ad-hoc bundle signing and ZIP packaging pass for macOS arm64, version 2.0.1.
- Read-only audits against local current-version data and older backup logs pass. Modern token totals were independently reconciled; missing historical logs and legacy estimates remain visible.
- Native UI checked: overview, date/model grouping, chat selection and request inspection, turn filtering, quota/reset timeline, word-frequency Chinese search, input-history search/expansion, backup discovery, migration running-process guard and the export dialog. No private logs or screenshots are included in this PR.

Migration compatibility was inspected against storage from `0.162.0-alpha.*` / `0.163.0-alpha.10.2` and desktop app `26.1013.40934`. Actual provider migrations were exercised only in temporary fixtures; endpoint connectivity and future storage versions are outside this validation.
